title: January 2016 event context
publicText: Civic Hall announced a January 30, 2016, 1-3 p.m. New York City Council hackathon focused on constituent services. An event-day Council post placed the gathering at Civic Hall and described it as the Council's first CouncilStat hackathon.
boundaryNote: The time range is an announced window. 'First' remains attributed to the Council. The archived carrier preserves embedded social posts and is not a recovered event listing.

title: Recovered event branding
publicText: A New York City Council-branded promotional graphic used the wording 'New York City Council Hackathon.'
boundaryNote: The graphic supports recovered event branding, not a longer formal registration title.

title: Independent CallNYC follow-on
publicText: After the complete constituent-services data became public, Jamie independently developed CallNYC.org as a resident-facing interpretation of the records.
boundaryNote: CallNYC was not an official Council product, formal hackathon submission, adopted service, or current public service.

title: CouncilStat interpretation limits
publicText: Politico reported Council staff's caution that offices used CouncilStat differently and entered information with different frequency.
boundaryNote: Recorded case totals cannot be treated as a simple measure of office quality, specialization, or resident need.

title: Politico New York coverage
publicText: Politico New York covered CallNYC on March 14, 2016.
boundaryNote: Coverage does not establish official Council ownership, adoption, or current-service status.

title: Public implementation repository
publicText: The public GitHub repository preserves the CallNYC implementation history.
boundaryNote: Repository existence does not establish official Council status, adoption, or current service availability.
